summary: The fix diff closes R1-1 to R1-6 as their plans described: the handled list reaches every round that ran the pass with the match sentence on its own gate, a field-less array stops as drift, the accounting runs after the carry-forward reconcile and counts each candidate where the round puts it, the findings file keeps the candidate list, and the handoff sentence is accurate. What remains is on the edges of the coverage contract (a renamed id losing its accounting entry, the marker parse, the meaning of `fixed` in the definition of new) and in what the docs and changelog promise about the pass (the guard's main-session approvals reach the skill fork; a setup rerun does not write models.coverage). No routes/console.php exists, so no scheduled or queued work applies; the version is already 0.2.0.

findings.title: The definition of new settles a re-found bug into an earlier finding marked fixed, even when the bug still reproduces at this head
findings.description: The candidates block (line 1162) and the reviewer's "New carries the run's done rule" paragraph (agents/redline-reviewer.md) list `fixed` among the outcomes a candidate collapses into. The fix-diff recheck looks only for bugs the fixes introduced, so nothing checks for a bug a fix left in place. If an implementer's fix covers one of two paths, the finding is still recorded `fixed`. A later coverage pass can re-find the other path at the new head, but the verifier is told to settle that candidate, the round confirms nothing new, and the run ends with the bug in the code. Re-verified at bac0b25, the head this round's review (already posted as R2-1) was made at; traced from the prompt text. How often it fires depends on how complete the fixes are.
findings.proposedFix: Decision needed: should a candidate that matches an earlier finding marked `fixed`, but still reproduces at this head, count as new (keeping the run going), go under For the person with the earlier id named, or stay settled as written? If new, add a sentence to candidatesBlock (line 1162) and to the reviewer's paragraph saying so, with deferred, decided, dropped and left-to-the-person findings still settled, and a loop-test check that the sentence is in the candidates block.

findings.title: The skill-denied and skill-absent markers match only as bare text at the very start of the reply
findings.description: coverageCandidates tests /^coverage: skill denied/i and /^coverage: skill absent/i against the start of the whole trimmed text, with no m flag (lines 1192 and 1195). The coverage prompt (line 1179) shows each marker inside backticks. A reply that copies the backticks, or opens with a sentence before the marker line, matches neither marker and holds no fenced array, so the round stops with the recipe-drift message (check `claude --version` against 2.1.318) instead of "Allow the Skill tool for this session". The parse is traced; whether the agent wraps the marker depends on the model.
findings.proposedFix: Test the markers only when no fenced list in the skill's shape was found, and match each at the start of any line with optional leading backticks or quotes, e.g. /^[ \t]*[`'"]*coverage: skill denied/im and the same for absent (denied first). Add loop-test cases for a backticked marker and for a line before the marker; each should stop with its own cause at coverage r1.

findings.title: A finding the workflow renames loses its accounting entry, so its candidate is also listed under For the person
findings.description: review() renames any finding id without this round's prefix (lines 1994-1998) but leaves the refs in out.coverage as the reviewer wrote them. Since the R1-4 fix, accountCoverage builds byId from the renamed ids (line 1249), so a `finding` entry naming the old id is treated as naming no finding: its candidate's summary is pushed under For the person and it is counted `forThePerson` (lines 1268-1274). A reviewer returning finding "r2-1" (renamed R2-1) with coverage {index 1, outcome finding, ref "r2-1"} gets R2-1 posted inline and the same candidate under For the person, and the count sentence says 0 confirmed. Introduced by the R1-4 fix; traced.
findings.proposedFix: Record old id -> new id in the rename loop and, before accountCoverage runs, rewrite out.coverage refs naming a renamed id (`finding` entries and `duplicate` refs that name an id). Loop-test check: finding id "X-1" with coverage [{index 1, outcome finding, ref "X-1"}] gives 1 confirmed, empty rounds[0].forThePerson, and the rename warning unchanged.

findings.title: The changelog says a setup rerun offers models.coverage, but a rerun keeps the existing models block
findings.description: The Setup and templates group is, by the file's own header, what a rerun of /redline:setup carries into a repository, and line 13 says a rerun "offers the new key". On a rerun, `redline-setup.sh config` updates only checker, checkerStallMs and (with --ask-rules) askRules and keeps every other value as the person's (scripts/redline-setup.sh header lines 72-74; skills/setup/SKILL.md line 109): models.coverage is only listed under `differs` as part of the whole models object, and the one way to take it is --force, which drops every hand-set value. A repository set up under 0.1.x never gets the key from a rerun; it runs with the pass on anyway, since absent means on.
findings.proposedFix: Reword line 13 to say what happens: the template gains `models.coverage`; an existing redline.json is left as it is (absent means on, at the first-round reviewer's model and effort), and a rerun lists the template's models under differs without writing them.

findings.title: The docs say the guard is inert in the coverage fork, but it approves every Redline script there without a prompt
findings.description: "What the guard does not vet" says the guard is inert inside the skill fork, that the pass's safety is the skill's read-only recipe and the session's permission mode, and that everything but read-only git meets the allow list or the permission prompt; README.md line 101 (Known limits) says the same. redline-guard.sh sends any Bash call from an agent with no Redline agent_type whose text names a Redline script, checks.sh or git to its main-session row (lines 43-60, 184-189), and that row returns an allow decision for every redline-gh.sh subcommand (lines 1070-1072, `main` in GROUPS), all of redline-prefs.sh (1079) and the repository's checks.sh (1064); tests/guard-cases.tsv rows 392, 394 and 407 pin those approvals. The coverage agent and its fork read the PR's untrusted diff, so a write subcommand of redline-gh.sh run from the fork (one that posts, replies, edits the PR body or resolves threads) is approved with no prompt, in a default-mode session too. Before this PR no non-role agent read PR content inside a run, so the exposure is new and the documented safety claim is wrong. Traced through the guard; the guard cannot be run by hand from this role.
findings.proposedFix: Decision needed: (a) correct running.md line 56 and the README's Known limits to say the guard approves Redline's own scripts and checks.sh for the fork exactly as for the main session, and accept that; or (b) also ask a person to narrow the guard's main-session row (a guard change a Redline run may not make). Note for (b): the fork carries no agent_type, the same as the main session, so the guard may not be able to tell them apart; any narrowing would also apply to the main session's own redline-gh.sh calls. Either way the docs change is the in-run part.

forThePerson.text: A `forThePerson` outcome is accepted without a matching For the person entry. If the verifier accounts a candidate there but lists nothing, the body still counts it and nothing shows it. The workflow cannot match entries to indexes exactly, so any check would have to guess, for example by file.

accountCoverage checks only `finding` refs: a `duplicate` ref naming no index or id (or two duplicates naming each other) and a `settled` ref naming no earlier id are recorded as given, so such a candidate lands in no list with no warning. R2-3's fix already rewrites duplicate refs; resolving them (and settled refs against history and the handled list) could fold in.

coverageCandidates takes the first fenced json array, and an empty one counts. If the skill's text held an empty array before the real list, the round would run on zero candidates. Not observed, since the contract is one array, but preferring the last array would close it cheaply.

The stop messages say "launch again with coverage off". From the session that stopped, the launch offers Resume first (and `claude -p --resume` resumes), and a resume ignores the typed word. A fresh headless session fails run check and starts fresh. The message could tell the person to pick Start fresh.

The pass is on by default, a denied Skill tool stops the round, and neither templates/settings.allow.json nor /redline:setup adds a `Skill(code-review)` allow entry or warns that one is missing; if Claude Code prompts for the Skill tool from a workflow agent, a default-mode or headless run set up under 0.1.x stops at coverage r1 until settings.json is edited by hand. Not reproduced here.

The reviewer role does not disallow the Skill tool, though checker and github do. Its instructions name the code-review skill, and docs/guard.md says a skill fork runs outside the guard. The gap predates this PR, but given the PR's own Known limits, adding `Skill` to disallowedTools seems worth it.
Two `finding` entries that name the same finding both count as confirmed, so the body's confirmed count can exceed the findings posted. The second should have been a `duplicate`.

On a fix-diff round the prompt calls the fix diff "The diff to review", while the guards say "inside the diff". The guard's "code this pull request did not change" points at the PR's diff; saying "the PR's diff on GitHub" outright would remove the ambiguity.

On fix-diff rounds the candidates block says the Version check in the reviewer's instructions "still applies", while that rule is scoped to a whole-PR review; adding "on a whole-PR round" there would keep a verifier from reading it as a Version check on every round.

The coverage agent is asked to retype the skill's whole result "complete and unchanged" though the workflow reads only the fenced array; on a large candidate list a truncated or mis-copied relay is reported as recipe drift. Asking for the fenced block alone would halve the output and that risk. Not observed.

personLine posts For the person text verbatim, and an unaccounted or bad-ref candidate is the skill's raw summary; a bare `@param`-style word in one becomes a GitHub @-mention. Reviewer-written finding text has the same exposure today; one escape where Redline writes GitHub text would cover both.

With the coverage pass on, the handoff's "the last one found no correctness bugs" could use the done rule's own words, "confirmed no new correctness finding". A bug the last round settled into a deferred finding is listed under Deferred either way.

In the human-review pass, the final nit pass's round record has no forThePerson field. Entries the reviewer returns there appear in the posted body but not in result().rounds. The main loop's record (line 3265) keeps them.
The cap-hit comment does not gather the rounds' For the person entries, so a capped run never gives the teammate the whole list in one place the way the handoff does.

When the coverage agent relays "Skill execution completed" (the known non-deterministic swallow), the no-array message blames recipe drift and the Claude Code version. Naming that text and suggesting a plain resume would spare the person a needless upgrade or coverage off.

The R1-3 drift check passes an array whose entries keep summary but rename file and line, so the candidates reach the verifier at `:0`. The summaries still carry the text, so only the location is lost.
baseArgs sets coverage to null, so the dial, revise-only, human-review, ask-rule and thread-sweep scenarios never run with the coverage pass on, which is the shipped default.

The mock reads scenario.coverage by round number but coverageOut by review order, so with firstRound 2 round 3's pass returns [] and its scripted accounting is ignored with two warnings. The check still holds (an empty pass is a pass), but `coverage: [undefined, two, two]` would script what the scenario says.
`models.coverage && typeof models.coverage === 'object'` repeats the launch check. `models.coverage ? 'coverage' : 'reviewerFirstRound'` does the same job.

Already tracked in the round 1 review's For the person (the skill gets no base). The line it lacks: the skill gets the branch name, not the round's SHA. Under `no push`, a skill that resolves the branch through GitHub or origin samples the old pushed head instead of the local fix commits.

Already tracked in the round 1 review's For the person (the skill gets no base). The line it lacks: it bites with a stale local main, not only a non-main base. In this checkout local main is e957077 and origin/main dfc9190, so main...HEAD spans 34 files against the PR's 29, and every pass samples already-merged code; passing origin/<base> or the PR number would fix it.

The `/redline:redline-review` argument-hint and description leave out `coverage off`, although a review-only run's coverage stop tells the person to launch with it (the R1-1 standard covers only the main skill and the alias).

accounting.ref: Dangling duplicate and settled refs: true by trace, but the workflow trusts the verifier's outcomes generally; listed for the person beside R2-3's fix.
No Skill allow entry in setup; depends on Claude Code's Skill permission behaviour, not reproduced.
Already tracked in the round 1 review's For the person (no base); the stale local main line added, confirmed in this checkout.
Unescaped @ in posted text; the same exposure exists for all reviewer-written text, rare for the raw-summary path.
Wording ambiguity: the sentence points at the instructions' Version rule, which carries its own whole-PR scope.
Mock indexing mismatch confirmed by trace; the check still exercises an empty pass, so it is test tidiness, not a missed regression.
Relay cost and truncation risk; a design trade-off from #79 Decision 5, not observed.

list.summary: accountCoverage() checks only `finding` refs. A `duplicate`, `settled` or `known` entry is recorded and counted with no check that its ref points at anything, so a candidate collapsed into a missing id, or into another duplicate in a cycle, ends up in no list, with no warning. The verifier's collapse is the run's stop rule, so the run can end on it.
list.failure_scenario: Round 2 has two coverage candidates. The reviewer accounts {index 1: duplicate, ref '2'} and {index 2: duplicate, ref '1'}, or {index 1: settled, ref 'R1-9'} where R1-9 never existed. Checked in a scratch harness: status=done, rounds=2, forThePerson=[], no warning (only the head-differs line). Both candidates disappear, the body says '2 collapsed into findings already reported or settled', and the run hands off with a possibly new bug unreported. The design's rule is 'never drop a candidate silently', and R1-4 fixed this only for `finding` refs.

list.summary: The docs say the guard is inert inside the coverage pass and that its other commands meet the permission prompt. That is wrong: for any agent without a Redline agent_type, the guard's main-session path actively approves every redline-gh.sh subcommand, all of redline-prefs.sh, and .claude/redline/checks.sh. Those calls get no permission prompt.
list.failure_scenario: The coverage agent has no agent_type, and neither does its skill fork. Both read the PR's untrusted diff with no guard. If either runs `<pluginRoot>/scripts/redline-gh.sh comment|reply|post-review|update|resolve-threads|request-review ...`, `redline-prefs.sh run save|clear`, or `.claude/redline/checks.sh` (which runs the PR's code), redline-guard.sh lines 1070-1084 return an allow decision, even in a default-mode session. Text in the PR can therefore post comments, rewrite the PR body or resolve threads as the author. The same wrong claim is in README.md:101 ('the session's permission mode'), docs/guard.md:7 ('the guard inert') and the new scripts/guard.md standard.

list.summary: The coverage pass now defaults on for every installed repository (a redline.json without the key means on), and the workflow treats a denied Skill tool as a stop. Neither the settings template nor setup adds a `Skill(code-review)` allow entry, and the precheck never warns that one is missing.
list.failure_scenario: After updating the plugin to 0.2.0, someone runs `/redline <pr>` in a default-mode or headless (`claude -p`) session in a repository set up under 0.1.x. The coverage r1 Skill call either prompts from a background workflow agent or is denied. The run stops at stage review with 'the Skill tool was denied' before any review is posted, until the person edits settings.json by hand. templates/settings.allow.json carries no such entry, and /redline:setup reports nothing for it.

list.summary: Already tracked in round 1's For the person (the skill gets no base). What that entry lacks: this checkout shows the range going wrong in the common case of a stale local `main`, not only on a PR that targets another base.
list.failure_scenario: Here, local `main` is at e957077 and `origin/main` is at dfc9190 (PR #78 merged). The skill, given only `xhigh <headRef> --max-findings all`, diffs against local `main`. This review hit exactly that: `main...HEAD` covers 34 files, including the already-merged #72 spike spec and standards, where the real PR has 29. Each pass then returns candidates on code outside the PR, which the verifier has to account for as `outside` or For the person, and the same happens again every round. Passing `${pr}` or `origin/${baseRef}` to the skill would fix it.

list.summary: personLine() posts For the person text verbatim into the review body and the handoff comment. Unaccounted candidates and bad-ref candidates are pushed as the skill's raw `summary`, with no rewriting by the reviewer, so a bare `@word` becomes a GitHub @-mention.
list.failure_scenario: On a PHP/Laravel PR, the skill writes a summary such as 'the @param docblock says int but @var says string' and the reviewer leaves that index unaccounted. accountCoverage pushes the summary as-is (lines 1272, 1297), and the review body and the handoff post '- `app/x.php:3` · the @param docblock ...'. GitHub notifies the users `param` and `var`. Nothing in the workflow wraps or escapes `@`.

list.summary: On fix-diff rounds, candidatesBlock tells the verifier the Version check 'still applies'. The reviewer's Version rule is limited to 'a whole-PR review', so the reviewer gets conflicting instructions every later round.
list.failure_scenario: Round 2 is a fix-diff round with candidates. A verifier that follows the prompt re-runs the Version check against the whole PR. If the version is unchanged and nobody dispositioned that nit in this run's history (for example, the run started at firstRound > 1), it reports a nit. A round with no correctness findings and that nit then becomes a nits-only round, which means an extra revise pass and a final nit pass. A verifier that follows agents/redline-reviewer.md instead skips the check. Either way, behaviour depends on which instruction the model obeys.

list.summary: The mock looks up scenario.coverage by round number (from the `coverage r<n>` label) but scenario.coverageOut by reviewer call order. In the firstRound: 2 handled-findings scenario, round 3 therefore gets zero candidates and its accounting is ignored, so the test does not exercise what it claims.
list.failure_scenario: handledScenario(true) (line 1339) sets coverage [two, two] with firstRound 2. coverage r2 reads index 1 and coverage r3 reads index 2, which is undefined, so it gets the default empty array. The re-review r3 accounting {1: settled, 2: outside} hits 'not an index of this round's 0 candidates; ignored' twice. Checked in a scratch harness: candidates per round [2, 0]. The check passes only because Array.isArray([]) is true. A regression that shows the handled list only when candidates are non-empty would stay green.

list.summary: The coverage agent must retype the skill's whole result 'complete and unchanged', but the workflow reads only the fenced JSON array. That doubles the pass's output tokens, and any truncation or mis-copy is reported to the person as recipe drift.
list.failure_scenario: On a large PR (for example 30 or more candidates at --max-findings all), the agent re-generates the skill's prose plus the JSON. If it hits its output limit, or 'tidies' a quote inside a summary, the closing fence is lost or JSON.parse fails. coverageCandidates returns 'no array', and the run stops with 'the skill's recipe may have drifted ... check claude --version', which is the wrong fix. Asking the agent to relay only the fenced json block would halve the cost and the risk.

list.summary: The changelog says a rerun of /redline:setup 'offers the new key'. It does not: on a rerun, redline-setup.sh config updates only checker, checkerStallMs and askRules, and keeps the existing models block as the person's.
list.failure_scenario: A repository set up under 0.1.x reruns /redline:setup. `models.coverage` is never written. The rerun only shows the whole `models` object under `differs`, and the only way to adopt it is `--force`, which rewrites the file from the template and drops every hand-set value (reviewer, askRules). The person reads the changelog as 'the rerun adds the key', which it does not. Absent still means on, so the line overstates what setup does.
